subject: Discovery recap: observability + evals — PeakHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@peakhealth.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@peakhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: observability + evals — PeakHealth

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture the next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Summary / pain points we heard
- Production latency spikes and tail latency variability during peak hours (affects chat assistants and document generation flows).
- Cost unpredictability across self-hosted models and cloud proxies — hard to plan for month-to-month spend.
- Lack of reliable regression detection for model updates — manual tests are slow and miss edge cases.
- Limited per-route observability: current Grafana dashboards are aggregated and don’t show token-level cost or model-version traces.

Current stack you described
- Self-hosted LLM endpoints behind an API gateway
- Redis caching for short-term KV/state
- Prometheus + Grafana for infra metrics; tracing via Lightstep for application traces
- CI runs lightweight smoke tests but no structured eval harness

Success criteria for a POC / evaluation
- Observable: per-route token/cost dashboards and 95th percentile response time <200ms for priority routes under defined load profile.
- Quality: golden prompt sets and automated regression alerts that surface degradations within 24 hours of a rollout.
- Safety & rollout: canary rollouts with automatic rollback if regression threshold exceeded; tracing hooks that map requests through to model version and prompt inputs.
- Cost: reduce per-token unit cost (or effective cost after caching/batching) ~25-35% for the main document generation route.

Specific asks you requested
- Dashboards: per-route token counts, per-route cost breakdown, model-version breakdown, and a dedicated eval dashboard for golden prompt results.
- Tracing: request -> model-version linkage, KV cache hit/miss tags, and sampled trace examples for slow requests.
- Evals: we’ll provide a CSV template for golden prompts + expected metrics (we discussed precision/recall proxies and generation-quality human spot checks).
- Regression alerts: daily automated checks with Slack/email alerts + an on-call escalation flow.
- Rollout guardrails: canary size suggestions, automatic rollback criteria, and a manual override path.

Next steps (action owners)
- Marissa (Redwood): share discovery deck + evals template (attached) and a HubSpot summary.
- Connor (Redwood SE): propose an infra footprint for a 2-week POC (small eval harness + 2 test workers) and confirm tracing hooks required.
- Maya / Oliver (PeakHealth): share a prioritized list of 3 golden prompt families and identify the stakeholders for quality sign-off.
- All: schedule a technical scoping call — suggested Wed 7/15 or Thu 7/16.

Attachments: discovery-deck-peakhealth.pdf, evals-template-peakhealth.csv

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

redwood.com

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, this looks right to me. A few quick clarifications:
- We can prioritize three prompt families: intake summarization, payer-response generation, and clinical note drafting. I’ll send the sample prompts by EOD.
- Regarding success criteria, the 95th <200ms is aggressive for document generation — if we can hit 95th <300ms at peak and show consistent reduction after caching/batching, that will be a meaningful win for us.
- For stakeholders: I’ll loop in our ML lead (sending contact in the next email) and our infra lead for provisioning network/VPC access.

We’re good to aim for the Wed 7/15 scoping call — please share a time that works for the team.

– Maya
Maya Srinivasan

Great recap, Marissa. I’ll take the lead on the POC infra and tracing work. Plan:

- Instrument tracing hooks to surface model-version and prompt input metadata (we’ll sample traces for slow requests).
- Wire up daily regression runs using the attached evals-template-peakhealth.csv.
